title: Git Examples
description: Small Git examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Meet local version history
examples.description: Version control records changes over time. Git can work on your own computer without a hosting service.

examples.title: Start a practice repository
examples.description: A repository is a project whose history Git tracks. Initialise only a new practice directory for this lesson.
examples.code:
mkdir learning-git
cd learning-git
git init

examples.title: Inspect the working tree
examples.description: The working tree is the set of files you edit. status tells you what is new, changed or ready for a commit.
examples.code:
printf "My first note
" > note.txt
git status

examples.title: Stage the intended changes
examples.description: The staging area holds the changes you intend to put in the next commit. Add only the files you mean to include.

examples.title: Make a local commit
examples.description: A commit records the staged snapshot with a message. Git needs a name and email label, which are part of the commit metadata.
examples.code:
git config user.name "Practice Learner"
git config user.email "learner@example.test"
git commit -m "Add first practice note"

examples.title: Read a difference
examples.description: A diff shows how current content differs from another version. Review it before saving the next version.
examples.code:
printf "A second line
" >> note.txt
git diff

examples.title: Read the history
examples.description: The log lists commits. The short view helps you see their order and messages without opening each snapshot.

examples.title: Try an idea on a branch
examples.description: A branch is a movable name pointing to a line of commits. It lets you work on a change without immediately adding it to another branch.

examples.title: Understand merging
examples.description: A merge joins histories. If two branches change the same lines differently, Git may need a person to choose the result.
examples.code:
git log --oneline --all --graph
# Read the graph before deciding what to merge.

examples.title: Ignore generated files
examples.description: A .gitignore file lists patterns Git should ignore when files are not already tracked. It is useful for temporary output.

examples.title: Inspect remotes
examples.description: A remote is a named address for another repository. Viewing remotes does not upload or download commits.

examples.title: Share a clear change
examples.description: A good shared change has a purpose, a reviewed difference and a short explanation of checks. A hosting service can review it separately from local Git.
examples.code:
Purpose: add club meeting time
Review: only the intended note changed
Check: read the note and verify the time
Message: Add club meeting time
